title: The playbook, the reflector, the name screen, case memory and what a solver is shown (harness learning, H2)
request: The owner asked to continue the harness-learning plan to the end of H2: lessons drawn from graded attempts, screened so they never carry a variant's answer, kept as small deltas merged by code, and shown to a solver beside its task.
spec: Plan 'improve the harness so it learns', package H2 (Phase 9's 31.5 to 31.7 with the reports' additions): an ACE-style playbook with invariant and domain lessons and counters moved by code; a reflector with editor discipline reading codes only; a deterministic name filter and an edit cap; case memory without names; the playbook in the solver's first user message, never the system prompt.
plan: the contract in dclab_core: Bullet, Delta, Playbook, apply and build with ACE's rules, render within a budget
the store: an append-only delta log per family and lineage
the screen: names as whole words with underscores or spaces, scores, steps, codes, scope, length, three a run
the reflector: the first wrong step, the rules drafter by default, a model through a new capped purpose
case memory without names; the payload for a solver; the intern's first user message
drafting from learning variants only; the command; tests; the prompt gates rerun; the review

decisions.decision: A playbook is never edited: it is rebuilt from an append-only log of deltas
decisions.why: ACE's lesson that a rewritten playbook collapses; every change keeps its author, reason and time

decisions.decision: The rules drafter writes one general lesson per code from a fixed table; a model is optional and capped
decisions.why: lessons cost nothing and name nothing by construction; a model's drafts pass the same screen

decisions.decision: The reflector is sent codes and step verdicts only, never the table, a name, a value or the key
decisions.why: a lesson written from names passes by recall on the next variant of the same skin

decisions.decision: Case memory keeps codes, lesson ids and verdicts, never a name
decisions.why: the skins reuse names across variants, so a remembered name is a remembered answer

decisions.decision: Drafts are filed as drafts: no solver sees a lesson before H3's probe accepts it
decisions.why: a lesson that does not raise the grader's score is noise in every later prompt

decisions.decision: The playbook reaches the intern in its first user message, never its system prompt
decisions.why: the system prompt is the hash-gated file every change is measured against

change: dclab_core/playbook.py (new), dclab_core/contracts.py (registered), dclab_core 0.103.0 + CHANGELOG + schemas; dclab_rnd/learning/ playbooks.py, filter.py, reflect.py, cases.py, inject.py, drafting.py (new) and __main__.py (draft); dclab_rnd/prompts/reflector.md and playbook_intro.md (new); dclab_rnd/models/settings.py (the reflector purpose); dclab_rnd/agents/harness.py (its role); dclab_rnd/intern/loop.py (the playbook argument and the first message); tests/test_learning_h2.py (new); tests/test_model_data_limits.py (the reflector's limit); the prompt gates rerun (AEV-053, HRN-040). Also dclab_core/challenge_pack.py (names matched as words in any spelling) and dclab_core/variants.py (family_names); dclab_rnd/learning/scoreboard.py (the attempt's run id).

findings.defect: the rules drafter's own group lesson named two skins' group keys
findings.scenario: its example list (a customer, a patient, an account) on the support and clinic variants, where patient and account are the plain-named group keys
findings.cause: an example written from general words that the generator happens to use as column names
findings.fix: the lesson reworded with no skin's words; a test screens every rule lesson against twelve variants
findings.impact: the answer handed to the solver on those variants

findings.defect: the new purpose had no data-limit test
findings.scenario: tests/test_model_data_limits.py lists every purpose with its test
findings.fix: a test: the reflector is sent codes and verdicts only, no cell value and no column name of a marked table
findings.impact: an untested channel to a model

findings.defect: the screen checked one variant's names while the playbook serves the whole family
findings.scenario: a lesson naming the household key passed on a customer variant, and every skin repeats across the partitions: the next household variant reads its answer
findings.fix: every lesson screened against every name the family's generator can use, across all skins, with the identifier prefixes

findings.defect: other spellings of a name passed the screen
findings.cause: a match on underscores and spaces only
findings.fix: text and names compared as words: CamelCase split, every other mark a space, the joined form too
findings.impact: a name through in another case

findings.defect: the model's drafts skipped the editor rules
findings.scenario: a draft answering a code the attempt did not fail, or one already answered, or citing the wrong step, was filed
findings.cause: the rules were applied in the rules drafter only
findings.fix: the editor's rules as code for a model's drafts; the step must be where the code's mistake first shows

findings.defect: the cap was cumulative over the challenges and a reached cap crashed the command
findings.scenario: one client for n challenges: the spend never reset; BudgetExceeded unhandled
findings.cause: the Bound's spend counts its whole life
findings.fix: spend reset before each challenge and totalled; a reached cap or a failed provider ends that challenge with no lesson and its reason
findings.impact: a traceback and no report after a few challenges

findings.scenario: a whole number, a percentage or an identifier's value passed
findings.fix: any digit refused (the rules' lessons have none)

findings.defect: nothing screened a bullet at the store's door
findings.fix: the store refuses an addition that fails the family-wide screen
findings.impact: a lesson unscreened in a solver's prompt

findings.defect: a forged id could replace another bullet's text and reset its counters; a status could skip the probe or go back
findings.scenario: add a different text with an existing id; draft to accepted
findings.cause: the id was not tied to the text; statuses had no order
findings.fix: a bullet's id must be the hash of its scope and normalised text; a status moves one step forward

findings.defect: the run's link to what it was shown and cited, the attempt's run id, and the reflector's own work were not recorded
findings.scenario: cited_in never called; Evidence.run None; refused drafts only on stdout
findings.cause: the records were planned but not wired
findings.fix: the session keeps the shown text's hash and the ids it cited; the attempt returns its run id; every draft is kept with its fate in learning/drafts.jsonl; the reflector is a recorded role step
findings.impact: a measured run not traceable to its lessons

findings.defect: the budget was exceeded by the cases' header and line breaks
findings.scenario: the test allowed ten tokens over
findings.fix: the header and breaks counted; the test holds the budget exactly

measurements.name: drafting from six learning variants in a scratch workspace
measurements.gate: lessons filed only for the codes the baseline fails on, each screened, all drafts
measurements.result: two lessons filed from the first failed attempt (the repeated entity, the decoy); later attempts with the same codes added none; one attempt passed and taught nothing; after the review's fixes every learning test so far and the prompt and harness gates pass
measurements.next: H3: the probe decides which drafts become accepted
limits: the rules drafter only; a model's drafts were tested with a scripted reply

outcome: Graded attempts on learning variants become screened lessons in an append-only playbook, with codes and ids as their only link to the attempt; a solver is shown the accepted ones in its first user message, under a budget, and its citations of them are found afterwards.
lessons: Screen a lesson against every name the generator uses, not only the variant it came from: skins share names.
Write a playbook as a log of deltas: its history is the evidence a promotion needs.
risks: no lesson is shown to a solver yet: H3's probe must accept one first
a drafted lesson is only as general as the codes: two different mistakes under one code get one lesson
the playbook is stored in files only: a PostgreSQL store through storage/ is open
ACE's pruning of never-used lessons is not built (H3 measures use first)
a learner run across processes appends under a thread lock only; build() re-applies the rules, so a stale delta is refused on read
